description: The cell is the fundamental structural and functional unit of life. Cytology and Genetics are crucial for understanding the formation, functioning, and transmission of hereditary traits in living organisms, forming a core part of competitive exams.

sections.title: Basic Principles of Cytology
sections.description: Important historical discoveries and fundamental concepts related to the study and classification of cells.

historical_events.event: Discovery of the Cell by Robert Hooke
historical_events.significance: He observed dead cells in a piece of cork and described them in his book 'Micrographia'.

historical_events.event: Discovery of the Living Cell by Antonie van Leeuwenhoek
historical_events.significance: He first observed free-living cells in pond water and is also considered the father of Microbiology.

historical_events.event: Cell Theory by Schleiden and Schwann
historical_events.significance: States that all living organisms are composed of cells, with viruses being a notable exception to this theory.

key_concepts.explanation: Primitive cells that lack a well-organized nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. Examples: Bacteria and Blue-green algae (Cyanobacteria).
Advanced, fully developed cells that possess a distinct nucleus and all membrane-bound cell organelles. Examples: Plant and Animal cells.

sections.title: Cell Organelles and their Specific Functions
sections.description: Common nicknames and primary functions of various cell organelles, frequently asked as direct or matching questions.

key_associations.extra_info: Generates energy in the form of ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) through cellular respiration.
Contains powerful hydrolytic enzymes capable of digesting and destroying damaged or dead cells.
Composed of RNA and proteins; it is the primary site for protein synthesis in the cell.
Found only in plant cells, containing chlorophyll to facilitate the process of photosynthesis.
Responsible for the modification, packaging, and targeted secretion of cellular materials.

important_facts.fact: The longest cell in the human body is the nerve cell (Neuron).
The largest single cell in the world is the Ostrich egg, while the smallest known cell is Mycoplasma gallisepticum.

sections.title: Cell Division
sections.description: Types of cell division and their critical roles in the growth, repair, and reproduction of organisms.

key_concepts.explanation: Occurs in somatic (body) cells. A single mother cell divides to produce two genetically identical daughter cells with the same number of chromosomes. It is essential for growth and tissue repair.

Occurs in reproductive (germ) cells. A single cell divides twice to produce four daughter cells, each with half the number of chromosomes. It is strictly essential for gamete formation (sperm and egg).

sections.title: Nucleic Acids: DNA and RNA
sections.description: Biological macromolecules responsible for the storage, transmission, and expression of genetic information.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: Proposed by James Watson and Francis Crick in 1953.
scientific_principles.application: Describes DNA as two intertwined polynucleotide chains held together by hydrogen bonds between complementary nitrogenous bases.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: Amount of Purines = Amount of Pyrimidines (A = T and G ≡ C).
scientific_principles.application: Adenine (A) always pairs with Thymine (T) via 2 hydrogen bonds, and Guanine (G) pairs with Cytosine (C) via 3 hydrogen bonds.

key_concepts.explanation: A single-stranded molecule primarily involved in protein synthesis. Unlike DNA, RNA contains the nitrogenous base Uracil (U) instead of Thymine (T).

sections.title: Genetics and Mendel's Laws
sections.description: The scientific study of heredity, transmission of traits from one generation to the next, and its foundational laws.

key_associations.extra_info: He conducted extensive hybridization experiments on the garden pea plant (Pisum sativum) to formulate the laws of inheritance.
Proposed that new species arise from sudden, large, and heritable genetic changes called mutations.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: In a cross between two pure-breeding parents with contrasting traits, only one trait (dominant) is expressed in the F1 generation.
scientific_principles.application: For example, in a cross between pure Tall and pure Dwarf pea plants, all F1 offspring are Tall.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: During gamete formation, the two alleles for a trait segregate (separate) from each other so that each gamete carries only one allele.
scientific_principles.application: This principle is universally accepted and is also known as the 'Law of Purity of Gametes'.

important_facts.fact: Every normal human somatic cell contains 23 pairs (46 in total) of chromosomes, comprising 22 pairs of autosomes and 1 pair of sex chromosomes (XX in females, XY in males).
The 'Gene' is the basic physical and functional unit of heredity. The term was coined by Danish botanist Wilhelm Johannsen in 1909.
